title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics, tool schema mapping, and tool message formatting (streaming stability)
author: Michael Park
description:
Summary: Implement OpenAI-compatible semantics for tool/function calling: (1) tool_choice resolution semantics (matching OpenAI's latest spec), (2) mapping between OpenAI tool schemas and Redwood's internal tool descriptor format, and (3) deterministic tool message formatting for streamed and non-streamed responses. This change also includes stability fixes for streaming tool messages so tool outputs are emitted in the correct role/order and addresses edge cases where partial tool outputs could break downstream JSON parsing.

Motivation: Customers using the OpenAI compatibility layer expect behavior consistent with the OpenAI function-calling experience (tool_choice selection, schema-constrained arguments, and tool-originated messages). In practice we saw mismatches during canary tests: (a) tool_choice was not surfaced correctly for multi-tool candidates, (b) schema mapping produced sanitized keys incompatible with some client validators, and (c) streaming emitted tool messages with intermittent role switches which broke client-side streaming parsers.

What this PR does:
- Implements tool_choice semantics: when model suggests a tool choice we emit the compatibility layer fields (tool_choice.name and tool_choice.metadata) and ensure Canary routing honors explicit tool selection for deterministic routing.
- Adds a tool-schema mapper that converts OpenAI-style JSON Schema tool definitions to Redwood's tool descriptor format (type, required, properties with typed hints). The mapper preserves enum/const constraints and adds an explicit "redwood_schema_hash" to support deterministic caching and compatibility checks.
- Normalizes tool argument formatting: validates against the mapped schema and produces deterministic canonicalization (stable key ordering, whitespace normalization) to reduce false-positive regressions in quality monitoring.
- Streaming stability fixes: ensure tool-originated messages are streamed with the role "tool" and that partial chunks never change the role in-flight. Added a short buffering strategy for the first N bytes of a tool response to ensure JSON payload boundaries are respected for common tooling.
- Tests: unit tests for mapper/rules, integration tests for tool_choice routing, and e2e streaming tests that simulate slow-producing tools.
- Docs: updated docs/openai/tool-calling.md with examples showing tool_choice, schema mapping, and example client parsing.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement mapper and validation hooks
- [x] Add tool_choice semantics and telemetry
- [x] Streaming fixes + buffering strategy
- [x] Unit/integration/e2e tests
- [x] Docs and examples updated

Related: builds on prior openai-compat PRs (see pr-70654, pr-73456, pr-76120 in the repo). Linear: ENG-4201 (tooling compatibility), ENG-4210 (streaming stability).

Notes on backwards compatibility: The changes are additive for consumers of Redwood's native tool API. For customers relying on exact key ordering of tool argument JSON we document the canonicalization in the release notes; we do not consider this a breaking change but have flagged it for customers via console release notes.
